summary: End-to-end JWT auth verification. Backend: 7/8 auth tests pass (login success, login wrong-pw 401, /auth/me with Bearer, /auth/me no-token 401, /auth/me invalid-token 401, all protected endpoints work with Bearer). Frontend: 100% pass — Login screen gates panel, wrong password shows login-error, correct credentials store 237-char token in localStorage 'fayr_token' and load the Shell, sidebar shows all sections (Fayr Assistant, Customer Support, Operations, Finance, Admin), session persists across reload via /auth/me, all pages (assistant/support/operations/finance/frontend-ops/admin) load without any /api error responses (Bearer attached by axios interceptor), logout-btn clears token and returns to Login. ONE backend regression: brute-force lockout (429 after 5 fails) DOES NOT trigger in the deployed environment.

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout never fires. RCA: identifier is built as f"{request.client.host}:{email}" but requests behind the Kubernetes ingress arrive from multiple upstream proxy IPs (observed 10.79.142.2 and 10.79.142.5 in login_attempts collection); counter is split across proxy IPs and never reaches 5 for the same identifier. Sent 7 wrong-pw requests in a row → all returned 401, none 429. Fix: parse X-Forwarded-For / trust proxy header (e.g. request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for','').split(',')[0].strip() or request.headers.get('x-real-ip')) with a safe fallback to request.client.host, OR key the counter on email alone (with per-email rate limit).

minor.issue: locked_until is $set on every failed attempt rather than only when count crosses the 5 threshold; the 15-minute clock effectively resets on each fail. Works only because check_lockout also requires count>=5, but the intent-vs-implementation drift is worth cleaning up.

issues: Recharts warning: 'The width(-1) and height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0' — chart container renders with no size on first paint; add minHeight to ResponsiveContainer parent.

action_items: Fix brute-force lockout: derive real client IP from X-Forwarded-For (Kubernetes ingress puts real client behind multiple proxy hops so request.client.host varies). Alternatively rate-limit by email only.
Optional: set locked_until only when count reaches 5, not on every failed attempt.
Optional: fix ResponsiveContainer sizing on Admin metrics to avoid recharts width/height=-1 warnings.
critical_code_review_comments: AuthContext uses null/false/user tri-state correctly — Gate() renders loader while checking; on 401 from /auth/me it removes token and shows Login (good).
Axios interceptor in src/lib/api.js attaches Bearer from localStorage on every request — confirmed all 6 pages call /api with Authorization header, no 401s.
Server issues both Bearer JWT and httpOnly cookies (set_auth_cookies) — the frontend intentionally uses Bearer/localStorage; that's consistent. get_current_user accepts either.
Bug: brute-force identifier depends on request.client.host which is not the true client IP behind ingress; must read X-Forwarded-For.

rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout RCA: server.py `login()` builds identifier = f"{request.client.host}:{email}". In this Kubernetes/ingress environment, `request.client.host` sees the immediate hop (varies between 10.79.142.2 and 10.79.142.5 — verified in login_attempts collection). Because the identifier changes per request, the 5-strike counter is fragmented and never reaches the threshold in check_lockout. Reproduction: `for i in 1..7; curl -X POST /api/auth/login -d '{"email":"x@x","password":"w"}'` → all 401, none 429. Mitigation: use `request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for', request.client.host).split(',')[0].strip()` when building identifier.
